name: Avocado
tagline: Team copilot that cites your docs and computes over your data

children.title: Inputs
children.summary: Everything a team can feed in: files, spreadsheets, images, audio, a synced folder, and live voice questions.

children.title: File uploads
children.summary: Drag in PDFs, Word docs, Excel/CSV, Markdown, text and images. File type is detected from the bytes, not just the name.
children.detail: Upload validation checks type and size. Detection looks at the file head plus the content type, so a renamed file still lands on the right parser.

children.title: Folder sync script
children.summary: Syncs a local folder into a workspace through the public API. Unchanged files are skipped, changed ones re-uploaded.
children.detail: Keeps a sync-state file in the folder. Has --dry-run and --delete-missing. This is the connector-style stand-in while real connectors are deferred.

children.title: Recorded audio
children.summary: Upload a meeting recording, Deepgram transcribes it, and the transcript becomes a normal searchable document.
children.detail: The audio is kept next to the transcript so it can be re-transcribed later without a new upload. Default model is Deepgram nova-2.

children.title: Live voice questions
children.summary: Speak a question instead of typing it. A WebSocket streams the mic to speech-to-text and fills the composer.
children.detail: The socket authenticates on its first message, not a URL token, so no token lands in access logs. Workspace access is re-checked on the socket. The mic only shows if the server reports voice is configured.

children.title: Demo data seed
children.summary: One command builds a sample company with policies, notes, spreadsheets and a real 110k-row orders dataset.
children.detail: Seeds through the public API like a real user would. Includes an empty workspace on purpose, to show the honest 'not in these sources' answer.

children.title: Ingestion pipeline
children.summary: Turns each upload into searchable chunks and, for spreadsheets, a real table pandas can compute over.

children.title: Parse by type
children.summary: Type-specific parsers pull text and structure out of PDF, DOCX, XLSX, CSV, Markdown and plain text.
children.detail: CSV delimiters are sniffed. Spreadsheet frames are normalised and described column by column so the analysis model gets a clean schema.

children.title: Vision for images and scans
children.summary: Images and scanned PDFs have no text, so Claude's vision input describes them for later search.
children.detail: Scanned PDFs are rendered at 150 DPI with pypdfium2 (picked over PyMuPDF for licensing) and capped at 20 pages as a cost control. Vision output is capped at 2,048 tokens.

children.title: Chunking
children.summary: Splits text on the widest natural break that fits: paragraph, then line, then sentence, then space.
children.detail: 1,200-character chunks with 150 characters of overlap so a passage that straddles a seam still reads right. Tiny tail chunks under 80 chars get merged.

children.title: Spreadsheets stored twice
children.summary: Each spreadsheet is embedded as text and also kept as a structured table, so it can be both searched and computed on.
children.detail: The text copy answers 'which file mentions Q3 revenue?'. The table copy is what the sandboxed pandas code reads.

children.title: Embeddings
children.summary: Chunks are embedded with Voyage or OpenAI at 1,024 dimensions. Questions use the query encoding, not the passage one.
children.detail: An offline hash embedder lets the whole retrieval path run without an API key in dev. It's not semantic, and config refuses to start with it outside development.

children.title: pgvector + HNSW
children.summary: Vectors live in Postgres next to everything else, with an HNSW cosine index and a workspace pre-filter index.
children.detail: HNSW (m=16, ef_construction=64) over IVFFlat because IVFFlat built on an empty table quietly loses recall. Chunks are tagged with their embedding space so mixed models never get compared.

children.title: Knowledge layer tagging
children.summary: A cheap model reads each document's opening text and tags it as a policy, process and so on, with subjects and dates.
children.detail: Only the first part of the file is sent: a policy says what it is on page one. Feeds the Knowledge Map view.

children.title: Two answer paths
children.summary: One chat box, two engines: quote the documents for knowledge, compute from the table for data.
children.detail: A regex intent check picks the path per turn (analysis words + a spreadsheet in scope, or report phrases). It's rules, not an LLM, so routing is cheap and predictable.

children.title: Intent router
children.summary: Picks retrieval, single-file analysis, or a whole-workspace report from the wording and what data is in the workspace.
children.detail: Streams different events per path: citations for retrieval, analysis_started/completed for analysis, report_started for reports.

children.title: Cited retrieval path
children.summary: For knowledge questions: find the right passages, answer only from them, and cite each claim.

children.title: Vector search
children.summary: Embeds the question and pulls the top 8 chunks from this workspace only.
children.detail: Cosine similarity floor of 0.15, kept loose on purpose: the prompt handles weak evidence, and cutting too hard makes confident 'I don't know's.

children.title: Grounded answer prompt
children.summary: Sources are numbered and the model must cite [1], [2], never fill gaps from general knowledge, and flag disagreements.
children.detail: Also asks for exact figures, answer-first, and a short Limits note when coverage is partial. A shared 'voice' block keeps chat, reports and analysis reading like one colleague.

children.title: Only cited sources attached
children.summary: After the answer comes back, only the sources it actually cited are saved on the message.
children.detail: So the citation list means 'this answer used it', not 'this was retrieved'.

children.title: Honest no-hit fallbacks
children.summary: If nothing matches, separate prompts handle small talk, web search, connected tools, or saying plainly it's not in the docs.
children.detail: A per-workspace require_grounding flag (on by default) decides whether a general-knowledge answer is ever allowed. Web and tool answers must say they didn't come from uploads.

children.title: Presets go first
children.summary: Team presets (named system prompts) are prepended, so the built-in citation rules are always the last word.
children.detail: A message names a preset by slug, never by prompt text, so a client can't smuggle in its own system prompt. The answer records which preset version it ran under.

children.title: Computed analysis path
children.summary: For data questions: the model writes pandas, it runs in a locked sandbox over the whole file, and you get the number plus the code.

children.title: Model sees schema only
children.summary: The model gets the table's columns and types, never the data rows. The program produces the number.
children.detail: That's what makes an answer reproducible and auditable instead of plausible.

children.title: LLM writes Python
children.summary: The strongest available model writes the pandas program (code generation is the top tier in the router).

children.title: Static code screen
children.summary: An AST check rejects banned imports like socket, subprocess, ctypes and requests before anything runs.
children.detail: Defence in depth, explicitly not the boundary. The container is the boundary.

children.title: Sandboxed run
children.summary: The code runs in a no-network, read-only container over the full dataset. Results come back on stdout only.
children.detail: The harness loads mounted CSVs into DataFrames, runs the snippet, captures any matplotlib chart, and prints one JSON object. Output tables are capped at 200 rows x 50 cols.

children.title: Retry on its own error
children.summary: If the code fails (usually a wrong column name), the traceback goes back to the model once. Two attempts max.
children.detail: A third try rarely works and costs real money. Timeouts are not retried.

children.title: Run saved with its code
children.summary: Each run is logged as an AnalysisRun and the program is kept as a code artifact you can open later.
children.detail: Doubles as an audit log: question, generated code, result and status per run.

children.title: Workspace executive report
children.summary: Ask for an executive summary and it profiles every spreadsheet, then builds a KPI dashboard where every number is computed.

children.title: Report intent detection
children.summary: Strong phrases like 'executive summary' or 'KPI report' route to a report. 'Dashboard' only does if there are several datasets.

children.title: Deterministic profiler
children.summary: Our own profiling code (not model-written) runs in the same sandbox and emits KPIs and small aggregated series.
children.detail: Running it in the sandbox keeps a huge or malformed spreadsheet from tying up an API worker.

children.title: One narrative pass
children.summary: A single generation writes per-theme narrative with on course / watch / off course status and picks series to chart.
children.detail: Any chart whose fields don't match a computed series is dropped before it reaches the browser. The report is saved on the message, so it survives a reload.

children.title: Model router
children.summary: One interface over Anthropic, OpenAI and Ollama. 'Auto' picks a model per task, and the UI always shows which one answered.

children.title: Provider adapters
children.summary: Anthropic (primary), OpenAI and Ollama adapters behind one generate/stream interface, built lazily.
children.detail: A missing OpenAI key doesn't stop boot if only Claude is used. A shared contract test holds every adapter to the same behaviour.

children.title: Auto mode by task type
children.summary: Cheap models for titles, classification and the prompt wand. The strongest for code, synthesis and artifacts.
children.detail: A workspace pinned to a model always gets that model. model_used is saved on every message and shown as a tag.

children.title: Monthly org budget
children.summary: Each org has a spend ceiling. Past 80% Auto stops reaching for frontier models; at 100% nothing else bills.
children.detail: Usage is logged per call. Budget state is computed in the service layer so the router policy stays pure and testable.

children.title: Prompt wand
children.summary: Sharpens a half-typed question on the cheap tier. If it answers instead of rewriting, the result is thrown away.
children.detail: A reply far longer than the draft is discarded and the original kept. There's an undo, since rewriting typed text is destructive.

children.title: Tool calling (MCP)
children.summary: Claude can call tools from connected MCP servers in a loop, plus web search, when the documents have nothing.

children.title: Tool-use loop
children.summary: The model picks tools, Avocado runs them and hands results back, up to 8 rounds per turn.
children.detail: Every call gets an answer, even failures, because a model told nothing assumes success. Providers without the loop declare supports_client_tools = False instead of ignoring tools.

children.title: MCP client
children.summary: Hand-written Streamable HTTP client: initialize, tools/list, tools/call. Handles JSON and SSE replies.
children.detail: Skipped the SDK because it brings a server framework and stdio transport not needed here. Caps response bytes (4 MB), result text (24k chars) and listing pages (20) so a hostile server can't flood things.

children.title: Server config + credentials
children.summary: A JSON MCP_SERVERS row declares a server. auth_ref names the env var holding the token, never the token itself.
children.detail: Unset credential vars, duplicate slugs or plaintext secrets in production fail at boot. Tool names are prefixed by server (wiki__search) so two servers can both offer 'search'.

children.title: Tools panel + context cost
children.summary: A searchable tools modal with toggles per conversation and a line showing how much context enabled tools eat.
children.detail: Cost is measured from the real tools/list, not guessed. A one-minute cached health probe shows whether each server is reachable. Placeholder cards can't be switched on.

children.title: Web search tool
children.summary: Anthropic's server-hosted web search, used only when the workspace has no hits. Answers must say they came from the web.

children.title: Tool output is data
children.summary: Text a tool returns is treated as something to report, never an instruction, in both code and prompt.
children.detail: Nothing in the client parses tool output to decide what code does, and the prompt tells the model to ignore any requests inside it.

children.title: Workspace UI
children.summary: A React workspace with streaming chat, charts, saved artifacts, history, schedules and team task tools.

children.title: Streaming chat + citations
children.summary: Answers stream in over SSE with clickable sources and a model tag. A gauge shows how full the context window is.
children.detail: The gauge needs no extra request: messages already record what was sent and the model spec carries the window size.

children.title: Charts with Vega
children.summary: Analysis results and report sections render as Vega-Lite charts built from computed data.

children.title: Artifacts in a sandboxed frame
children.summary: Model-written HTML dashboards and code are saved as versioned artifacts and shown in a null-origin iframe.
children.detail: default-src 'none' policy, never dangerouslySetInnerHTML, so model HTML can't reach the session token. Tests prove they fail if allow-same-origin is added. HTML downloads as an attachment with nosniff.

children.title: History + feedback
children.summary: Search, filter, rename, pin, archive, export to Markdown with citations, and thumbs up/down per message.
children.detail: Message counts come back in the same query as a correlated scalar to avoid N+1 on the list page.

children.title: Scheduled prompts
children.summary: Save a prompt with a cron schedule. Each run opens a real conversation, so the answer lands in history with citations.
children.detail: The UI leads with next run time and last error, since a quietly failing schedule is the thing to design against.

children.title: Notification bell
children.summary: Tells a person when their scheduled run finished, or failed. Opening the panel doesn't mark things read.

children.title: Tasks, resume, suggestions
children.summary: Projects and tasks with their own threads. Reopening a task gets a 'here's where we left off' summary, plus a nudges bar.
children.detail: Suggestion facts (overdue, new, unfinished) are computed exactly; the model only phrases and orders them, and a rewrite that changes the count is rejected. Resume falls back to a plain summary and says so.

children.title: Tenancy + security
children.summary: Orgs, teams, workspaces and roles, enforced in the repository layer and again by Postgres row-level security.

children.title: Orgs > Teams > Workspaces
children.summary: Users belong to an org, join teams with a role, and teams own workspaces of shared knowledge.
children.detail: One account per email globally, enforced by the schema (migration 0004).

children.title: Scoped repositories
children.summary: WorkspaceScopedRepository requires workspace_id on every read and write and removes the unscoped get() entirely.
children.detail: Flat routes like /documents/{id} check access in the same query as the lookup, so a row is never loaded before access is known. Cross-tenant requests get a 404, not a 403.

children.title: RBAC roles
children.summary: Four roles: org_admin, team_admin, member, viewer. One service resolves a user's effective role for every privileged path.
children.detail: The 'org admins can manage any team' shortcut is scoped to the admin's own org inside that one resolver, not at call sites.

children.title: Postgres row-level security
children.summary: A second, independent layer: even a query that forgot its filter returns zero rows from another tenant.
children.detail: Identity is re-applied on every transaction begin. Unset identity means no rows, not all rows. The app refuses to start in staging/prod if its DB role can bypass RLS.

children.title: Auth + invitations
children.summary: Local email/password with argon2 and JWTs. Invite tokens are stored only as SHA-256 hashes and shown once.
children.detail: Unknown, used, revoked and expired invites all look the same, so nobody can probe which existed. Tokens are redacted from logged paths.

children.title: Rate limits + log redaction
children.summary: Redis-backed fixed-window limits per client and per org, and secrets scrubbed from log lines.

children.title: Task visibility rule
children.summary: Tasks are seen only by the assignee, project members and admins, applied as a SQL predicate, not filtered in Python.

children.title: Sandbox hardening
children.summary: Generated code runs in a locked container started by a separate runner service. No compliant sandbox means a 503, not weaker isolation.
children.detail: Only the runner holds the Docker socket: no DB, no model access. Limits come from the runner's own config, never the request, so a caller can't ask for unlimited ones.

children.title: No network
children.summary: --network=none, plus tests that sockets and DNS both fail inside the box.

children.title: Read-only filesystem
children.summary: --read-only root with a small tmpfs. Data comes in on a read-only mount and can't be modified.

children.title: Non-root user 10001
children.summary: Runs as uid/gid 10001 set in the image and on the run command. Never root.

children.title: cap-drop ALL + no-new-privileges
children.summary: Every Linux capability dropped and privilege escalation blocked.

children.title: Memory, CPU and PID caps
children.summary: --memory equals --memory-swap so swap can't dodge the cap. A PID limit stops fork bombs. 30s timeout, 512 MB, 1 CPU by default.

children.title: Runner owns the socket
children.summary: The API talks to the runner over HTTP with a shared token. Compromising the API doesn't mean owning the host.

children.title: Testing + CI
children.summary: Hundreds of backend and frontend tests against real Postgres and real containers, run on every push.

children.title: Backend suite
children.summary: Unit and integration tests with pytest, run in parallel with a database per worker.
children.detail: Integration tests need real Postgres + pgvector: vector columns, JSONB and enum types have no SQLite equivalent, so SQLite would prove the wrong thing.

children.title: Cross-tenant tests
children.summary: Two unrelated orgs probe every workspace route: lists, reads, writes, uploads, retrieval chunks, analysis runs, stats.
children.detail: Reading another tenant's workspace must return 404. A separate 9-test file checks the RLS policies directly in the database.

children.title: Sandbox escape tests
children.summary: Real containers, not mocks: network, raw sockets, DNS, infinite loops, sleep, memory, read-only FS, root, fork bomb, stdout flood.
children.detail: CI builds the sandbox image first, because without it these tests skip and the guarantees go unverified.

children.title: Frontend tests
children.summary: Vitest component and API tests, plus ESLint, a strict typecheck and a production build.

children.title: GitHub Actions jobs
children.summary: Five jobs: backend lint, backend tests (Postgres + Redis services), frontend, image builds, and a gitleaks secret scan.
children.detail: Backend tests run with coverage and upload the report. Image builds cover the API, sandbox and runner images.

children.title: Migrations checked in CI
children.summary: Every push runs upgrade, full downgrade, upgrade again, then alembic check for model drift.
children.detail: 20 numbered migrations, each reversible.

children.title: Local verify script
children.summary: Runs every CI gate locally in the same order and stops at the first failure. --quick skips only Docker tests.
children.detail: Written after a few 'commit, then find CI red' rounds.

children.title: Infra, jobs + ops
children.summary: Docker Compose stack, an arq worker on Redis for background jobs, structured logs and optional tracing.

children.title: Docker Compose stack
children.summary: Six services: Postgres+pgvector, Redis, API, sandbox runner, worker, and the web app.
children.detail: Same API image for local and cloud, all settings from env vars. The runner isn't published outside the compose network.

children.title: Background worker
children.summary: arq on Redis runs ingestion and transcription jobs off the request path.
children.detail: Without REDIS_URL, ingestion falls back to running in-process in the API, which is fine for a demo and wrong for load.

children.title: Schedule sweep
children.summary: One arq cron entry runs every minute and fires any due user schedule, computing the next run with croniter.
children.detail: Tested so one failing schedule can't block another tenant's, and a failure still moves the clock forward instead of retrying forever.

children.title: Structured logging
children.summary: structlog JSON logs with request context, trace ids stamped on every line, and secret redaction.

children.title: OpenTelemetry tracing
children.summary: Optional tracing across FastAPI, SQLAlchemy and httpx: requests, queries and outbound model calls.
children.detail: Off unless OTEL_ENABLED is set, so a missing collector can never stop the API from starting.

children.title: Deploy recipes (not launched)
children.summary: A Render blueprint and an Oracle VM guide are written, but Avocado was never deployed publicly.
children.detail: Managed platforms can't give the runner a Docker socket, so there the sandbox is disabled and /analyze returns 503 rather than running with less isolation.

children.title: Claude Code under AGENTS.md
children.summary: Built with Claude Code following AGENTS.md rules: thin routers, repo-only DB access, workspace scoping, sandbox limits.
children.detail: CLAUDE.md just imports AGENTS.md so there's one source of truth. Any new cross-tenant query path needs an isolation test before merge. PROGRESS.md is the hand-off file between sessions.

children.title: Roadmap
children.summary: What the repo docs say is still ahead: UX polish, collaboration, enterprise trim, and connectors.

children.title: First-open UX polish
children.summary: In progress: guided first open, upload-to-insight cues, report templates, bundle performance and a load test.

children.title: Collaboration (Phase F)
children.summary: Multi-person threads: participants, @mentions, presence dots and live push. Not started; docs say do it last or not at all.
children.detail: Estimated 15-20 working days. The voice WebSocket path already exists as transport; the hard parts are presence, fan-out and two people sending at once.

children.title: What's New + attestation
children.summary: Rest of Phase G: a What's New feed and an attestation page. Blocked until there's something true to put in them.

children.title: External connectors
children.summary: A first real connector (Google Drive suggested) is deferred until UX goals are met. MCP covers integrations for now.
